description:
## What the warning says

```
warning[type/no-matching-clause]: `fn` clauses don't cover every input
  --> runtime:Enum.fz:469:3
    |
469 |   fnp split_sort_list([left_head, right_head | tail], left, right) do
    |   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the last clause is here
    |
    = note: an input matched by no clause halts with `:function_clause` at runtime
    = help: add a wildcard clause `_ -> ...` to cover any remaining input
```

The function's clauses are `[]`, `[single]`, and `[first, second | rest]`.

## Why a reader cannot act on it

A reader looks at those three clauses, sees every possible list, and concludes the compiler is wrong. It is not: the parameter has no declared domain, so it is `any`, and `split_sort_list(:atom, [], [])` genuinely matches nothing. But the message never says so.

Three things are missing or wrong:

**It does not name the uncovered input.** "don't cover every input" is the claim; the reader needs the counterexample. `an atom, or any value that is not a list` would end the confusion immediately.

**It does not mention the domain, or types, at all.** The actual fix is `@spec split_sort_list([a], [a], [a]) :: {[a], [a]}`, which silences it completely. Nothing in the diagnostic points there.

**The `help` recommends the wrong fix.** Adding a wildcard clause makes the warning go away by making the function total over `any` -- accepting values it cannot handle and returning something arbitrary for them, or panicking. That is the opposite of what the code wants, which is to say the parameter is a list. The help steers the reader toward suppressing the message rather than toward the declaration that makes it untrue.

That is not hypothetical: working on fz-5xp.81 I followed the help and added a terminal panic clause, and was told to stop coding around the warning and fix it properly. The diagnostic recommended the thing that had to be undone.

## What it should say

Name a value that reaches no clause. Say what the parameter's domain currently is and that it is undeclared. Offer the declaration first, and the wildcard only as the alternative for a function whose domain really is wider than its clauses -- which is the case for `Json.encode!/1` and almost nothing else in the library.

## Related

fz-5xp.87 declares the missing domains. This ticket is about the message that failed to ask for them.
title: [BUG] The clause-coverage warning names no uncovered input and recommends the wrong fix
